stem: A grocery chain wants to stop discovering empty shelves only when customers complain. Leaders want store managers to see sales and stock movements as they happen so replenishment can be ordered the same day. Which business value of data does this goal illustrate?

choices.text: Lowering hardware spending, so that the chain can retire a few older servers in its head-office building
Generating real-time business insights, so that managers can act on events while they are still happening
Archiving records for later audits, so that the chain can prove what was sold once each year has closed
Standardizing store layouts, so that every outlet displays the same products in the same positions

stem: An insurer's executives are surprised that a pilot AI claims assistant gives vague and sometimes wrong answers. The assistant was built quickly, but the claims records it learns from are scattered across departments, partly outdated and inconsistently labeled. Which statement best explains the situation in terms of the role of data?

choices.text: AI replaces the need for data, so the answers should have been correct even though the records were scattered and outdated
Data volume alone decides AI quality, so adding more outdated records from other departments would fix the answers
Data fuels AI, so the quality, completeness and accessibility of the data behind a model strongly shape how good its results are
Data matters only for reporting, so the pilot's weak answers must come from the interface the claims staff use

stem: A retail bank runs an application where customers transfer money. Each transfer must be recorded immediately and correctly, and thousands of such small updates happen every minute. Separately, the finance team wants to analyze years of combined data from many systems for reports. Which pairing matches these two needs?

choices.text: A database for the transfers, and a second copy of that same database for the cross-system reporting
A data warehouse for the transfers, and a database for the cross-system reporting
A data lake for the transfers, and a database for the cross-system reporting
A database for the transfers, and a data warehouse for the cross-system reporting

stem: A streaming company collects clickstream logs, video thumbnails, support-call recordings and sensor files. Its data scientists do not yet know what questions they will ask, and they want the original raw data kept as it arrived so they can experiment with machine learning later. Which approach fits best?

choices.text: A data lake, which stores large amounts of data of all types in its native format without a predefined schema
A traditional on-premises warehouse that accepts only cleaned and structured tables from a nightly batch load
A transactional database with a fixed schema, so that every file is converted into rows before it is stored
A spreadsheet shared by the data scientists, where each file type is summarized into columns by hand

stem: A leadership team is deciding how to describe the difference between a data warehouse and a data lake to the board. Which TWO statements are accurate? (Select TWO)

choices.text: A data warehouse stores only video and images, while a data lake stores only numeric tables
A data lake and a data warehouse can never be used in the same company because their data cannot be combined
A data lake always requires every record to be fully cleaned and modeled before any data can be stored in it
A data lake can keep raw structured, semi-structured and unstructured data in its native format for analytics and ML
A data warehouse is optimized for repeatable business reporting and structured SQL analysis of cleaned data

stem: A furniture retailer wants to personalize its newsletter using the purchase history, website browsing behavior and loyalty-program sign-ups that it collects directly from its own customers. How is this data classified?

choices.text: First-party data, because the retailer collected it itself from its own customers and channels
Third-party data, because it describes people and so must come from an outside data aggregator
Public data, because anyone browsing the retailer's website could in principle see all of it
Second-party data, because it is about customers who each belong to a different retailer

stem: A hotel group and an airline agree to exchange anonymized booking data about travelers who have opted in to partner offers, so that each can design joint travel packages. From the hotel group's point of view, the data it receives from the airline is which kind?

choices.text: Third-party data, because the airline is another company and not the hotel group's customer
Second-party data, because it is the airline's own first-party data shared directly under a partnership agreement
Unstructured data, because exchanged booking data has no defined fields and cannot be analyzed by query
First-party data, because the hotel group now holds the records inside its own storage

stem: A marketing director wants to reach people who are not yet customers. The agency suggests buying an audience list of demographics and interests that a data aggregator compiled from many sources and sells to many advertisers. What kind of data is this, and what should the director weigh?

choices.text: First-party data, so the director can assume it is accurate because it is held in company records
Structured data only, so the director needs no checks because every field has a fixed meaning and format
Third-party data, so the director should weigh how accurate, consented and relevant it is, since the buyer did not collect it
Second-party data, so the director can expect it to be exclusive because only one partner supplied it

stem: A logistics company receives shipment events as JSON messages. Each message has labeled fields such as "shipmentId" and "status", but different carriers add different extra fields, and there is no single fixed table design. How is this data best described?

choices.text: Structured data, because a labeled field in a message proves that the data belongs in fixed rows and columns
Unstructured data, because anything that arrives as text messages carries no recognizable organization
Semi-structured data, because it has labels and organization but does not follow a rigid, fixed table schema
Unlabeled data, because the extra carrier fields mean that nobody tagged the data with the correct outcome

stem: A city transport authority wants to map its data supply chain. It starts with the moment a passenger taps a card on a bus reader, which creates a travel record that did not exist before. Which stage of the data supply chain is this?

choices.text: Data analysis, the point at which people or systems examine data to find patterns and answers
Data activation, the point at which insights are put to work in an action, product or process
Data processing, the point at which raw records are cleaned and transformed into a more useful form
Data genesis, the point at which data is first created or generated by an event, device or interaction

stem: A manufacturer's dashboards show inflated production counts. An investigation finds that sensor readings reach the central system correctly but include duplicates, readings in different units and missing values, and nothing fixes these before the data is stored. At which stage of the data supply chain is the gap, and what does it call for?

choices.text: Data processing, which needs cleaning, de-duplication and standardization before the data is stored and analyzed
Data collection, which needs the readings to be delayed so that they arrive less often at the central system
Data activation, which needs the dashboards redesigned so that managers see fewer production counts
Data genesis, which needs the sensors replaced so that the readings are never created in the first place

stem: A telecom company's analysts have built a model that predicts which subscribers are likely to cancel. The company now wants the call-center system to automatically show an agent a retention offer whenever a flagged subscriber phones in. Which data supply chain stage does this represent?

choices.text: Data analysis, where the model is trained and the cancellation predictions are first produced from the history
Data activation, where analytical results are fed into a business process or customer experience to drive action
Data collection, where call events are first gathered and brought in from the telephone system
Data storage, where the subscriber history is kept in a system that the analysts are able to query

stem: A bank describes its data supply chain activities. Which TWO of the following correctly pair an activity with its stage? (Select TWO)

choices.text: A customer opening a new savings account, which creates a brand-new record in the system, is data analysis
Building a dashboard of last quarter's loan trends is data collection
Loading daily branch transactions into a data warehouse for analysts to query is data storage
Cleaning mismatched date formats across the bank's regional systems is data genesis
Sending a list of high-value customers to the email platform for a targeted campaign is data activation

stem: A multinational has analysts in different countries who each keep their own copies of customer data in separate tools. They disagree on revenue totals, nobody is sure who may see personal data, and a regulator has asked how the company controls sensitive records. Which approach addresses all three problems?

choices.text: Data governance: shared standards for how data is gathered, defined, accessed, protected and used throughout its life cycle
Data deletion: removing all customer records so that no one is able to see personal data
Data hoarding: keeping every copy that each team has made, so that no team ever has to give up its own version
Data duplication: giving every analyst a private copy so that nobody depends on another team's version

stem: A company's leaders are debating whether to fund data governance, because some executives see it as only slowing teams down. Which TWO benefits of governance should the data leader cite? (Select TWO)

choices.text: A requirement that all data be stored in a single location regardless of regulations
Removal of the need for any data catalog, labeling or ownership of data
Guaranteed elimination of every security incident without any further technical controls
Safer self-service access, so more analysts can use governed data without exposing sensitive records
Trustworthy, high-quality data that reduces unreliable insights and AI answers

stem: A software company stores its analytical data in a proprietary format that only its current vendor's engine can read. Moving to a different engine would require rewriting and re-exporting years of tables. Leaders want a data platform that avoids this lock-in. Which approach reflects Google Cloud's openness?

choices.text: Keeping the proprietary format but adding another vendor's license to use as a backup in a future migration
Storing data in open table formats, such as Apache Iceberg, so that multiple engines can analyze the same data
Allowing only one approved engine for the whole company so that nobody ever needs to ask about moving
Converting all data to image files so that no analytics engine in particular is able to depend on it

stem: After acquiring two companies, a retailer finds sales data in one cloud, customer data in an on-premises system and product data in a third vendor's service. Reports need weeks of manual exports because the systems cannot share data easily. Which design principle best addresses this problem going forward?

choices.text: Standardizing on one closed ecosystem, so that every future acquisition must first rebuild its data in the vendor's format
Interoperability through open standards and connectors, so data can move and be queried across systems without manual copying
Isolation of each system, so that every department keeps strict control over its own data and rarely shares it
Printing the weekly reports from each system, so that employees can combine the results by hand

stem: A publisher's board asks why it should invest in a central data platform when editors already trust their instincts about which stories readers like. The data lead wants an argument based on identifying trends and informing strategic decisions. Which response fits?

choices.text: A central platform is valuable mainly because it prevents anyone outside the editorial team from ever viewing any readership figure
Reader data should be collected only for legal record keeping, since it cannot influence which stories the publisher chooses to commission
Editors' instincts are always more accurate than readership data, so the platform would be used mainly to store their conclusions
Analyzing reading behavior across years and topics can reveal trends, such as rising interest in a subject, so that investment decisions rest on evidence
